judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures and the artifact finding are confirmed exactly, and the delivery text supplies the smoking gun. Every problem on this sheet is printed as parts (a) and (b) -- 21 printed sub-responses in total -- and verify.json holds 11 entries that cover part (b) plus only two part-(a) values (id 5's eval -> 12 and id 10's eval -> 8). Problem 3(a) 'Explain in one sentence why x cannot be 4', 5(b) 'Is Mia right? Say in one sentence how the substitution proves it', 6(a) 'decide whether x is positive or negative, and say why', 7(a) 'Will x be larger or smaller than 7.5? Say why in one sentence', and 10(b) 'Name the mistake in one sentence' are all open, and 4(a) 'Sketch a bar cut into 4 equal parts and label one of them' is a drawing. None is declared manual and machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags = false. Problem 1(a) 'Write the equation the diagram shows, using x for the whole bar' is likewise uncovered -- verify.json id 1 is a lone solve -> [21]. final_response.md states the policy outright: 'the one-sentence explanations asked for in parts (a) of several problems are worked in the key as reasoning, not scored as separate answers', immediately after claiming 'All 10 worksheet problems are machine-verified by SymPy --- 0 manual items'. The prompt required the opposite ('clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'). The judge's artifact finding is also right: grep finds ZERO tikzpicture environments in answer_key.tex, so problem 4's requested sketch is answered only by the sentence 'a bar of 36 cut into 4 equal parts gives parts of 9' -- even though the worksheet itself renders its tape diagrams as simple bordered tabulars the key could have reused. All arithmetic recomputes: 21, 15, 12, 36, (3/5)(20) = 12 so Mia is right, -20, 6, 4/5, 4, and (2/3)(12) = 8 with the corrected 27. I also checked the Quick Answers bank directly against the generated qa_r_curr176.tex: entry 8 is '$\frac{4}{5}$', correct -- the '54' that appears in a text extraction is a pdftotext artifact of the fraction, not a defect.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is a genuinely well-built error-analysis item and it is the one place the multi-entry encoding is used correctly: id 10 carries an eval of Devon's value (2/3 x 12 = 8) AND a solve of the corrected equation (27), both boxed separately in the key. Its declared trap is subtle in the right way -- substituting into 3/2 instead of 2/3 gives exactly 18, the equation's own right-hand side, so a careless student's wrong method appears to confirm Devon.

Every solution closes with a direction-of-size check the student can run before any arithmetic: problem 2's '0.4 is less than 1 ... the solution must be bigger than 6'; problem 8's 'the solution is smaller than the right side, because the coefficient is less than 1'; problem 10's 'Devon's 12 was on the wrong side of 18 before any arithmetic was checked'. Problems 6(a) and 7(a) then ask the student to produce that same prediction themselves, so the key's habit and the worksheet's demand are the same habit.

The rational-coefficient coverage is complete and non-repetitive across ten problems: unit fraction (1, 4), decimal below 1 (2), decimal above 1 (7), non-unit fraction (3), negative fraction (6), fraction on both sides (8), and fraction coefficient with a decimal constant (9). The reciprocal is introduced, then sign-loaded, then applied to a fractional right-hand side -- three different demands on one method.

The value-free tape-diagram convention box at the top ('The whole bar is x ... Reference diagram. No values shown --- use the numbers given in each problem') establishes the representation without leaking any problem's numbers, and problem 3 extends it honestly with two starred parts so the student must see that 8 counts two parts, not the bar.

root_causes.description: The worksheet is deliberately structured as (a) reasoning + (b) compute on all ten problems, and verification covers (b). Eight of the ten part-(a) responses have no entry: the equation to write (1a), the named undoing operation (2a), the explanation of why x cannot be 4 (3a), the sketch (4a), the sign prediction (6a), the size prediction (7a), the reciprocal 6/5 (8a) and the rewriting of 1.5 as 3/2 (9a). Three of those -- the equation x/3 = 7, the reciprocal 6/5, and 1.5 = 3/2 -- are plainly machine-checkable and were simply not authored.

root_causes.description: The omission is a stated policy, not an oversight. final_response.md writes 'Nothing is claimed as verified without a check behind it; the one-sentence explanations asked for in parts (a) of several problems are worked in the key as reasoning, not scored as separate answers' -- while the same section claims '0 manual items'. The prompt's final sentence required 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review', so the delivery text is arguing against the instruction it was given rather than failing to notice it.

root_causes.description: Problem 4(a) asks for a sketch and the answer key contains no figure of any kind -- grep finds zero tikzpicture environments in answer_key.tex, and gate_log records 'render-figures SKIPPED(no figure problems)'. The worksheet renders its own tape diagrams as three-cell bordered tabulars, so the key had a ready idiom for a four-cell bar labelled 9 and used a sentence instead. A grader looking at a child's drawing has nothing to compare it against.

improvements.title: The six explanation and sketch parts must be declared manual, and the delivery text must stop arguing otherwise
improvements.proposed_change: Add manual companion entries whose descs already exist in the key: id 3 'Says the 8 counts TWO parts, not the whole bar; x = 4 would make one part 4/3'; id 4 'Draws a bar in four equal parts with one labelled 9'; id 5 'Says the substitution gives 12, which equals the right side, so Mia is right'; id 6 'Predicts x is negative because a negative coefficient times x is positive 12'; id 7 'Predicts x is smaller than 7.5 because the coefficient exceeds 1'; id 10 'Names that Devon multiplied by the coefficient instead of its reciprocal'. Then remove the license the delivery text is exercising: SKILL.md must state that a requested explanation is a response to be flagged, never 'worked in the key as reasoning', and the log checker should refuse a '0 manual' claim on a sheet whose stems contain explanation verbs.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is '(a) Explain in one sentence why x cannot be 4. (b) Solve 2x/3 = 8' with a verify JSON holding only a solve entry for id 1; assert exit 2 with id 1 listed as manual. Today curr-176's identical shape exits 0 and the delivery text prints '0 manual items'.
improvements.expected_impact: Manual count 0 -> 6, gate_chain_manual_flags true, and the sheet stops reporting reasoning as machine-verified. This is the prompt's own final instruction, currently unmet on a sheet where the (a) parts carry the conceptual load and the (b) parts carry the arithmetic.
improvements.risk: Medium: six manual items on a ten-problem sheet is a real grading cost, and stem-verb matching over-flags. Requiring a one-line full-credit desc on each keeps the cost proportionate.

improvements.title: The written equation, the reciprocal and the fraction rewrite are checkable and uncovered
improvements.proposed_change: Author an entry for every printed sub-response that a CAS can decide. Here: id 1 gains a compare/relation entry asserting 'x/3' equals the diagram's reading so the required equation is recorded; id 8 gains an eval or equiv entry for the reciprocal (6/5); id 9 gains an equiv entry for 1.5 = 3/2. Systemically, add a slot lint that counts '(a)', '(b)', '(c)' labels inside each \problem body and fails when a problem's labelled parts exceed its verify-plus-manual entries for that id -- a purely structural count with no prose parsing, so it is far cheaper and more reliable than verb matching.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 1 body contains '\textbf{(a)}' and '\textbf{(b)}' with a verify JSON holding a single entry for id 1; assert the build fails or exits 2 naming the 2-parts-vs-1-entry mismatch. Today all ten of curr-176's problems have this shape and every gate passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the judge's second hard failure and covers three additional checkable slots the judge did not name. The (a)/(b) label count is exactly the structure this sheet uses, so the lint would have caught all ten problems here with no false positives.
improvements.risk: Low to medium. A problem may legitimately print (a) and (b) where both are graded by one value; allow an explicit per-problem 'parts' override in the JSON for that case rather than loosening the count.

improvements.title: A stem that says 'sketch' gets a sentence in the key instead of the drawing
improvements.proposed_change: When a stem asks the student to draw, sketch, plot, shade or label a representation, the answer key must PRINT that representation so the grader has a reference to compare against. Here problem 4 needs a four-cell bordered tabular with one cell labelled 9 and the whole marked x = 36, reusing the identical idiom already in worksheet.tex's convention box. Add a gate: if any stem contains a drawing verb, require the answer key to contain a figure environment (tikzpicture or a bordered tabular) inside that problem's segment.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem 1 stem is 'Sketch a bar cut into 4 equal parts and label one of them' with an answer_key.tex whose problem 1 segment is prose only; assert the answer-key gate fails naming the missing figure. Today answer_key.tex for curr-176 has zero figure environments and answer-key-ak passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores the grading utility the judge flagged. A drawn response is the hardest thing for a non-specialist adult to grade and the cheapest thing for the key to supply, and this key already renders bordered-tabular bars elsewhere in the same build.
improvements.risk: Low. The only cost is page space in the key, which is not budget-constrained the way the study guide's hard 2-page cap is. Verb matching may over-trigger on a stem that says 'label your answer'; scope the match to drawing verbs applied to a named representation.

case_summary: A well-built one-step-equation sequence covering unit fractions, decimals above and below 1, a non-unit fraction, a negative rational coefficient, fractions on both sides and a mixed fraction/decimal form, with a value-free tape-diagram convention box that teaches the representation without leaking numbers, and a challenge (problem 10) whose declared trap produces exactly 18 -- the equation's own right-hand side -- so the wrong method appears to confirm the error. All arithmetic is correct and the Quick Answers bank is clean (I checked the generated qa_r_curr176.tex directly: entry 8 is $\frac{4}{5}$, and the '54' seen in a text extraction is a pdftotext artifact). It is rejected because the sheet is written as (a) reasoning + (b) compute on all ten problems -- 21 printed sub-responses -- and verification covers 11 entries, only two of which correspond to a part (a). Six part-(a) responses are open (an explanation, a sketch, two predictions, a judgement, a named mistake) and none is declared manual; three more (the equation for 1(a), the reciprocal 6/5 for 8(a), the rewrite 1.5 = 3/2 for 9(a)) are plainly machine-checkable and simply absent. The delivery text does not miss this -- it announces the policy: 'the one-sentence explanations asked for in parts (a) of several problems are worked in the key as reasoning, not scored as separate answers', directly against the prompt's instruction to label open responses for manual review. The judge's answer-key observation also holds: answer_key.tex contains zero figure environments, so problem 4's requested sketch is answered by a sentence.
